findings.title: Sender check crashes when integration metadata has no sender
findings.body: GitHubInstallation unconditionally evaluates integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]. Integrations created before sender was recorded, created through build_integration when state has no sender, or otherwise lacking that nested key will raise KeyError/TypeError here instead of rendering the installation-failed page. This produces a 500 and blocks legitimate attempts to attach an existing orphaned Integration (no OrganizationIntegration) to an organization.

findings.title: Authenticated-user check is bypassed when the Integration row does not yet exist
findings.body: When Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist, GitHubInstallation returns pipeline.next_step() without comparing pipeline state github_authenticated_user to the installer. Because the GitHub webhook that creates the Integration (with sender metadata) is asynchronous and can lag the user's redirect, an attacker who knows/guesses an installation_id and authenticates to GitHub as a different user can complete the pipeline in that window; build_integration only fetches /app/installations/{id}, which contains no sender to validate against, so the PR's mismatch protection is race-dependent and ineffective for fresh/racing installs.

findings.title: Token exchange and user lookup failures are not converted to the error page
findings.body: safe_urlopen at line 423 is outside the try/except (only safe_urlread/parse_qsl is guarded), and get_user_info(payload["access_token"]) at line 434 is also unguarded. A network error, GitHub HTTP error, invalid/reused code causing a failed /user call, or a missing code (e.g. user denies authorization, so code is None and form-encoding/exchange can fail) will raise and return a 500 instead of the documented 'We could not verify the authenticity...' installation-failed response.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the installation-not-found path
findings.body: The updated test_installation_not_found drives the setup endpoint with state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, which fails OAuthLoginView's pipeline-signature check and renders 'Invalid installation request.' before GitHubInstallation/build_integration ever calls get_installation_info. The stubbed 404 for /app/installations/{id} and the IntegrationError 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' path therefore have no coverage, so a regression in that handling would not be caught.
